title: What Happens in the 2 Seconds After You Tap Your Card
description:
ZERO just got his first credit card. He taps it for a $4.75 coffee, the terminal says APPROVED in under two seconds, and he has no idea who just agreed to pay for him. So time stops, and he rides the payment through the shop's side, the card network and his bank's risk room, where a brand-new card looks suspicious. Then he stays until night to see when the money really moves, and who takes a cut.

Zero doesn't know how the world works. Yet.

Chapters
0:00 ZERO's first credit card
0:28 Three companies in two seconds
0:40 What the card really sends
1:33 First stop: the shop's side
2:01 The card network
2:52 ZERO's bank
3:19 Why a brand-new card looks suspicious
4:33 Approved. But nothing was paid
5:12 Tonight: who owes whom
5:54 Who takes a cut of $4.75
6:41 Who really pays for it
7:04 The bill
7:28 What ZERO understood

Every number in this video has a source. FACT = stated by the source; ESTIMATE = our calculation or a model's estimate, rounded; ILLUSTRATION = how it can look, not a real bank's rules.
- A contactless card has no battery: the terminal powers its chip; every chip payment makes a one-time code (FACT): Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, "Contactless Payments in the U.S.", 2019 https://www.bostonfed.org/-/media/Documents/PaymentStrategies/payment-strategies-contactless-report-2019.pdf
- Shop's processor → card network → your bank; 258 billion Visa transactions in fiscal 2025; stand-in processing when a bank can't answer; redundant data centers; 16 billion+ tokens (FACT): Visa Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal 2025 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1403161/000140316125000089/v-20250930.htm
- About 8,200 transactions a second on average (ESTIMATE, our calculation from the 10-K; average, not peak).
- The first digits of the card number (BIN) say which bank issued it (FACT): Visa, "8-digit BIN expansion" https://usa.visa.com/content/dam/VCOM/regional/na/us/partner-with-us/documents/visa-8digitbin-expansion-issuer-processors.pdf
- 500+ risk details weighed in about a millisecond (FACT, Visa's own claim, 2019): Visa press release, Jun 17 2019 https://usa.visa.com/about-visa/newsroom/press-releases.releaseId.16421.html
- The whole approval takes about 1-2 seconds (ESTIMATE): Monzo, "The 3 second sandwich", Dec 2 2015 https://monzo.com/blog/2015/12/02/3-second-sandwich/
- How ZERO's bank weighs his new card (ILLUSTRATION): each bank's model is private; the video shows how it can look.
- Approval only reserves the money; the shop batches the day's payments and is usually paid in 1-2 business days (FACT): Forte, "Credit card payment lifecycle" https://support.forte.net/support/solutions/articles/11000132030-credit-card-payment-lifecycle
- One net settlement per bank per business day (FACT): Visa Developer, "Settlement" https://developer.visa.com/capabilities/dps-payment-account-solutions/settlement
- Average US credit interchange about 1.9%, mostly funding rewards; about $30 billion a year moving from cash and debit users to credit card users (FACT / ESTIMATE from an academic model): NBER Digest, Jul 2026, "Who Ultimately Pays Credit Card Interchange Fees?" https://www.nber.org/digest/202607/redistributive-impact-credit-card-interchange-fees
- All the slices on a $4.75 coffee ≈ 10-15¢ (ESTIMATE): 1.9% ≈ 9¢ plus network and processor fees; small-ticket pricing varies.
- US merchants paid $187.2 billion in card processing fees in 2024 (FACT): The Nilson Report https://nilsonreport.com/articles/merchant-processing-fees-in-the-united-states-2024/
- Debit fees at large banks are capped (Regulation II); credit card fees are not (FACT): Federal Register, Nov 14 2023 https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/11/14/2023-24034/debit-card-interchange-fees-and-routing
- Rewards cards carry higher fees (FACT): Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, Aug 2023 https://www.kansascityfed.org/Root/documents/9754/CreditDebitCardInterchangeFeesVariousCountries_August2023Update.pdf
- Billing disputes under the Fair Credit Billing Act (FACT): FTC, "Disputing Credit Card Charges" https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-FT-PURL-LPS104618/pdf/GOVPUB-FT-PURL-LPS104618.pdf
- Pay the full statement by the due date and there is generally no interest; the bill arrives at least 21 days before (FACT): CFPB, "What is a grace period?" https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-grace-period-en-47/
- 22.36% average rate on accounts charged interest, Aug 2026 (FACT): Federal Reserve G.19, Oct 7 2026 https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/g19/current/g19.pdf
- $1.26 trillion in US credit card balances, Q2 2026 (FACT): New York Fed, Household Debt and Credit, Aug 11 2026 https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/news/research/2026/20260811
The café, the $4.75, 8:14 AM, the 312 payments, the man who pays cash and ZERO's 5¢ cash back are part of the story, not claims.
